opening: Murali Krishna Gumma, the head of GIS and Remote Sensing Lab at ICRISAT, co-authored a new paper that demonstrated the power of continental-scale mapping using 30-meter Landsat imagery data on Google Earth Engine. Applying the random forest machine learning algorithm, the team, led by Pardhasaradhi Teluguntla at U. S. Geological Survey, was able to generate the new cropland extent in Australia and China with the overall accuracy exceeding 94%. The data products are freely available from the USGS website at https://lpdaac.usgs.gov/node/1282. Mapping high resolution (30-m or better) cropland extent over very large areas such as continents or large countries or regions accurately, precisely, repeatedly, and rapidly is of great importance for addressing the global food and water security challenges. Such
continuation:
data can also be used for modeling and monitoring a number of phenomena, including crop yields and soil moisture status.

Australia's agriculture sector is an important contributor to the national economy and employs millions of people across the country. With a very diverse climate, the majority of agricultural production is concentrated in the southeastern part of Australia and mostly within a narrow strip less than 100 km wide from Sydney to Melbourne. The south-eastern part of Australia is mainly mountainous region, and a certain level of topographic variability can influence the land surface conditions. The rugged and complex topography of this region makes it challenging for the remote sensing practitioners to produce accurate maps.

The Landsat satellites have been providing valuable data for mapping and monitoring cropland extent for decades. In 1972, the very first Landsat satellite was launched by NASA and USGS, which provided various multispectral data. The spectral resolution of the Landsat data was coarse, and thus it may not be appropriate for mapping small cropland parcels. From 2013 onwards, Landsat-8 has been collecting optical data in 11 spectral bands with two new spectral bands in shortwave infrared (SWIR) region. The spectral resolution of the Landsat-8 data is better, and thus it is expected to be more suitable for high-resolution cropland mapping.

The authors developed a supervised machine learning model using the random forest classifier to classify cropland from other land cover types. The Landsat-8 images were collected over the study areas on two random dates selected from 2015. The study regions were divided into randomly assigned training and test areas with the training set used for model development. They collected ground truth data for cropland and other land cover types in their training areas using Google Earth.

The developed model was tested on the test areas and showed an overall accuracy of 94% for Australia and 95% for China. The model was able to correctly identify the cropland pixels with an overall producer's accuracy (PA) of 95% and user's accuracy (UA) of 95%. The methodology works well for topographically rugged areas, and thus a large extent of cropland across the entire Australia can be modeled.

"High-resolution land cover information is crucial for understanding crop growth and productivity as well as for monitoring land use, land cover change, and environmental impacts," said Krishna. "The research we conducted is a step towards obtaining such information at a continental scale for China and Australia."

The team also looked into the temporal dynamics of cropland extent. The results showed that cropland area in China increased rapidly over the time period, while cropland extent in Australia remained stable. opening: In the world of working stock dogs, there is no more iconic breed than the border collie. The quintessential sheepdog, the border collie can trace its ancestry to rough drover’s dogs used in the border country between England and Scotland from the 17th to the 19th century to work livestock and drive them to market. Despite being indispensable to the shepherds of these rugged and inhospitable highlands, the drover dogs of this era were neither easy to handle nor easy on the stock. In the late 19th century, a shepherd by the name of Adam Telfer began experimenting with a cross between these coarse dogs and the milder-mannered working collie. The end result was a dog by the name of
continuation:
Cynfael, whose descendants were used in 1906 to produce one of the early border collie pedigrees.
This breed was named in 1915 by the Kennel Club of Great Britain, which selected the name “border collie” because the dog originated in the border country between England and Scotland. The Kennel Club of America has recognized the breed since 1917, and it belongs to the Herding Group.
Breeders have given several nicknames for the border collie, including barbecue, black and tan, Herd-Dog and Scotch. The term barbecue comes from the traditional use of the breed as barbecue dogs, i.e. dogs that work outdoors and eat pork chops. Black and tan is a reference to the common color pattern of the breed. Herd-Dog also refers to the traditional use of this dog for work, while Scotch is a nod to the borderlands.
Border collies are active and intelligent dogs that require intensive exercise and mental stimulation. Many of these dogs excel in canine sports, including obedience and agility trials, and are also often used to help train other dogs.
Standard size: Males: 19-22 inches, females: 18-21 inches
Weight: Males: 30-45 pounds, females: 27-42 pounds
The border collie is medium-sized dog with a moderate bone structure and an athletic build. This dog’s broad chest and broad neck give it the appearance of a lion-like head, while its long neck and proud carriage accentuate its alert posture. The border collie’s legs are set well apart, giving the impression that it is on the verge of springing into action. The dog’s coat comes in a variety of solid and bi-color combinations, including black and white, blue merle, red and white, and others.
This dog’s medium-length coat may be short to wiry or long and soft, but it must never be silky. The coat is found in three lengths: short, medium and long. The long coat should be feathered on the ears and tail, and never appear to be shaved.
The border collie’s facial features are striking. The muzzle is long, straight and deep, with a moderate length and moderate width. The nose is well-pigmented in a color that matches the coat. The eyes are almond-shaped and set obliquely, with an intense expression. The ears are triangular and set high on the head, and they may be erect or folded back against the head. The border collie’s bite is level, with even, straight jaws and a scissor or level scissors bite.
This breed’s temperament is loyal, intelligent and agile, with a strong desire to please and a keen sense of observation. Border collies are active and energetic dogs that require regular exercise and mental stimulation. They also have a strong herding instinct, which can manifest in nipping or chasing smaller animals, including children and other dogs. However, with proper training and socialization, border collies can become well-behaved family pets.

opening: The Atholl Memorial Fountain in Dunkeld. The Atholl Memorial Fountain was funded by public subscription and built in 1866 'to the memory of George Augustus Frederick John 6th Duke of Atholl. The Fountain was funded by public subscription and built in 1866 'to the memory of George Augustus Frederick John 6th Duke of Atholl'. The Duke had introduced a piped water supply to Dunkeld, prior to which all water had to be drawn from the River Tay - hence all the wynds leading to the water. The Fountain was designed by C S Robertson and erected on the site of the Market Cross. Several changes are apparent over the years, but there is fine detail in the carvings, which include
continuation:
a figure of St John holding the Book of Prophecies - a nod to Dunkeld's claim as the home of St Columba. The Fountain was originally complete with four statues – Atholl, Duncan and his sister Mary, the Duke's father, and his uncle. The statues of the Duke and Duncan were removed at the start of WW1 as a sign of respect; Mary was melted down to create a bust which is now on display in Perth Museum; Duncan was also later destroyed, during the Jubilee celebrations for the King's 1897 Silver Wedding Anniversary. The Fountain is now topped by a statue of Athena, who won the 1897 Sculpture Competition. In 2009 the Fountain was refurbished and restored as part of a grant from the Heritage Lottery Fund.

The Tower House, Dunkeld. The Tower House at Dunkeld was probably built c1720 and designed by Robert Mylne. This was the family seat of the Dukes of Atholl and now houses a museum. The original castle is reputed to be one of the finest surviving examples in Scotland, but it was destroyed by fire and the present tower house was built in 1720 by Robert Mylne. It was then extensively remodelled and extended in 1815 by a private architect who added four rooms in the East Wing and the Georgian facade to the North. The building subsequently became known as Ardgowan House and was used as a residence for future Dukes of Atholl and their families. It is now housed in a museum, the Dunkeld Museum, dedicated to the history and archaeology of the area. The building is a Grade A listed building and has been owned by the Dunkeld Heritage Trust since 1978. The museum at Ardgowan House was opened on the 26th September 1985. It is a modern museum in the style of the building with extensive and interesting displays on some of the most important buildings and artefacts from the Dunkeld area.

Dunkeld Distillery. The Distillery is situated on a site which has had an association with the manufacture of spirits for hundreds of years. There is some evidence that the manufacture of whisky at Dunkeld began in medieval times, the highest recorded tax for a still house being for £25 in 1317. The 'Dunkeld Weir' was built as part of the canals in the 18th century to provide water to drive the mill that powered the stills. The original distillery was licensed in 1727, and it was subsequently leased to the Seathill Distillery who built a new, larger facility on the site in 1928. It was renamed "Dunkeld Distillery". The distillery was still producing drinks for sale in other countries when it closed in 1987. In 2002, the site was purchased by Highland Park and returned to production for an indeterminate period of time. The site is now owned by a private buyer and is being prepared for redevelopment.

opening: It’s safe to say that by now, most of us understand the importance of protecting our planet from environmental harm. We recycle, buy reusable water bottles, and donate items rather than throw them away. Some people take it even further and drive electric cars, use solar energy, and shop with businesses that have an eco-friendly mindset. But let’s face it, many of us are busy – and while we want to do our part, we want our contributions to be simple and practical. If you want to do more to help save the planet without too much work on your end, there are some simple changes you can make. They require a little effort upfront, but nothing over the top.
continuation:
1. Shop at Farmers Markets
For a time around Thanksgiving, most people flock to local farmers markets. This gives them an opportunity to buy organic produce and other goods directly from local growers. But many farmers markets stay open all year round, so it’s easy to make the habit a part of your routine. Not only is buying locally grown food convenient, but it’s also beneficial to local producers and can have a smaller environmental impact than supermarket produce.
2. Get a Reusable Water Bottle
Having to buy bottled water is incredibly expensive, and plastic water bottles are harmful to the environment. But carrying around a reusable bottle takes time and effort. The good news is that reusable water bottles are affordable, easy to find (even online), and can last for years. It’s a small step that makes a big difference.
3. Use Reusable Produce Bags
Don’t forget the produce! If you’re going to buy organic food, ditch the plastic bags and bring your own reusable bags. It’s simple to make this habit a part of your shopping routine, but it can save you money and reduce the amount of plastic waste in the world.
4. Buy Organic
If you want to make a difference, buying organic is a great way to do it. While the price may be a bit higher, you’re not just helping yourself – you’re also helping the environment and local growers. And if you want to make organic more affordable, consider buying in bulk or growing your own food.
5. Say No to Paper Bags
Next time you go shopping at a store and they ask if you want a bag, say no – unless you really need one. Most stores have a recycling program for their bags, so it’s even easier to reduce your use. If you do need a bag, consider using a reusable one for next time.
6. Say No to Plastic Bags
While you’re at it, say no to plastic bags as well. Most people have a reusable bag or two in their car or purse, so it’s easy to forget that you don’t need a plastic one. If you really do, see if the store offers a recyclable bag option.
7. Use Reusable Tote Bags
When you do need a bag, consider using one of the totes you have. If you’re shopping for groceries, take an extra tote in your car or bring a few with you. If you’re shopping for clothes, take a bag to carry your items in. If you don’t have any totes, consider buying some – it’s a small investment that will pay off in the long run.
8. Bring Your Own Utensils
When you’re out to eat, bring your own utensils and napkins. This way, you won’t be forced to use disposable ones that will end up in a landfill. If you don’t want to carry around your own, consider buying reusable ones that you can wash and use over and over again.
9. Use Reusable Coffee Cups
If you’re a coffee drinker, consider bringing your own cup to coffee shops. Many places offer discounts for customers who bring their own cups, so it’s a win-win situation.

Although, we strongly disagree with this point of view in general, occasionally the value of warehousing might be redundant as demonstrated by the following case study. Case Study: Office Supplies for Non-profit Organization A non-profit organization held a central inventory of office supplies. A study revealed that it would be cheaper and quicker if the various branches ordered the office supplies directly from the wholesaler. Apparently, the distribution center only incurred costs and increased response times. The organization immediately decided to terminate the distribution center. In most instances the distribution center does add value to the supply chain. Hence, it is important to understand

Role of Warehousing The role of the warehouse has evolved significantly over the years to become a major component of today's supply chains. Having central locations with large capacity, warehouses were often the most expensive parts of a manufacturing or distribution facility. With improvements in transportation and information technologies, many warehouses are now used for value-added activities rather than just storage. For example, a warehouse today may perform both storage and break-bulk operations, where large shipments are broken down into smaller shipments. A warehouse might be used to consolidate products from various manufacturing plants before distributing the products to retailers. Many warehouses now have high-tech sorting equipment which allows for quick and efficient distribution of individual orders to retailers. Warehouses may also be used to stage products for delivery to retail stores. This staging allows the retailer to receive several shipments in one delivery which saves on transportation and delivery costs. The distribution center also allows the retailer to restock its shelves more frequently and provide a better customer service. Retailers now use sophisticated information systems to communicate with warehouse management systems (WMS). These systems are used to generate pick lists, determine the optimal order quantity for each product, and even suggest where within the warehouse each item should be placed. These systems allow for a high degree of accuracy and efficiency. They also are the basis for real-time tracking of goods as they move through the warehouse and on to the customers. Warehouses today are nothing like they were even a few years ago. The introduction of sophisticated information systems has revolutionized the distribution center. Most warehouses now are managed by a computerized system that monitors and controls all warehousing operations. The system generates various reports, such as product usage, warehouse utilization, and order status. The reports allow the business to determine if any adjustments need to be made in the operations of the warehouse. For example, if the reports show that a particular product is used more frequently than other products, then the warehouse might decide to place the product in a more accessible location. They system also allows for simulation of different warehousing operations to determine the most efficient way to store and distribute products. The computerized system also allows for better coordination between the various departments of a business. The sales department can easily communicate with the warehouse on product availability, shipment status, and delivery schedules. The production department can communicate with the warehouse on inventory levels and resupply needs. The system also allows for better coordination between the various branches of a business, as it provides a central location that can easily coordinate distribution to each branch. The benefits of computerized warehouse management systems are numerous. They allow for a high degree of accuracy and efficiency in warehousing operations. opening: “Most Australians form their views on public issues, particularly those in relation to migration and diversity, from the mainstream media and political discourse. Simplistic, reductionist and negative reporting of African-Australian youths leads to whole communities being stigmatised to a point where it is acceptable for them to be publicly denigrated and ostracised,” Professor Mansouri said. Discover the entire article in which UNESCO Chair of Cultural Diversity and Social Justice / Professor Fethi Mansouri responds to a moral panic over ‘African gangs’ in Australian media narratives and called for contextualisation of the issues surrounding these sensationalised reporting. This report presents findings from a three-year Australian Research Council (ARC) Discovery Project. The project uses a comparative approach to explore the everyday experiences
continuation:
of young men and women who identify as ‘Africans’.
Since the emergence of “africanisation” following large immigration from sub-Saharan Africa in the 1980s and 1990s, a violent face of this concept has emerged. This narrative, which conflates African descent with violence, has permeated public discourse in Australia, and is evident in sporting incidents, election campaigns, parliamentary debates, school truancy rates, community unrest, and the domestic and international media. While “africanisation” is a common trope, it is driven by different agendas and played out differently. In this chapter, we explore “africanisation” through historical and contemporary examples of the federal government’s interventions to regulate street gangs. These interventions not only enable but also drive “africanisation” as they assume a racialised understanding of gangs, associating African descent with criminality. Following this, we examine the impact of policing in capital cities and regional communities in Australia. In our analysis of police strategies to disrupt street gangs, we find that the framing of “africanisation” drives and is driven by strategies of violence. We argue that the fear about “africanisation” is not only ignored but actively encouraged and exploited by Australia’s media and political leaders.
The first wave of sub-Saharan African (SSA) immigration into Australia in the 1970s was small and largely assimilated without significant disruption to Australian society. When large numbers of refugees from Central and Eastern European countries arrived in the 1980s, SSA immigration was dominated by a human rights agenda. Following the collapse of apartheid in South Africa, and increasing conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo, SSA immigration significantly increased. The arrival of asylum seekers in 2001 further intensified Australia’s already deepening fear of African descent. This fear has continued to drive public discourse and policy in relation to “africanisation”.
Contemporary fears about African immigration and the rise of street gangs is not new to Australia. These fears emerged in the early 1980s, and were almost certainly influenced by a media narrative that conflated African descent with crime. In 1982, a country town in Victoria experienced a tense period of racial conflict, exacerbated by a biker gang and a group of youths – some African-Australian and some Indigenous. The race riots that took place in the town were largely driven by an Anglo-Australian biker gang and a group of whites who spread fears about a violent African-Australian gang. These fears were then exploited by local politicians and the mainstream media.
It is no surprise that contemporary notions of “africanisation” emerged from a long history in Australia – one that conflates African descent with violence and places African-Australian citizens at the centre of fears about Australia’s national identity. These assumptions are manifest in contemporary policy responses to street gangs, and continue to drive and be driven by discourses of “africanisation”.
Government policy in relation to street gangs has not only perpetuated but also driven “africanisation”. The media narrative that conflates African descent with violence has become an integral part of Australia’s policy and legal responses to street gangs

opening: Languages at EOHS Why learn Te Reo/Māori? EOHS offers a Te Reo programme from year 7—10. During Year 7 and 8, students have a Te Reo lesson once a week for two terms. The programme is based on an odd/even year cycle. Even year focus is on Kai (food) and odd year focus is Te Marae (the marae). Alongside the Vocabulary and Tikanga of these topics students build a basic Kupu Hou (word bank) of greetings, simple questions about their families friends and classroom. The Year 9 programme builds on the basics covered in the junior school. They study sentence structure and simple conversations. Year 9 students have two periods of Te Reo for two terms. One group focus on
continuation:
the role of Te Reo Māori, the importance and the processes for revitalisation. The second group discuss aspects of tikanga (customs) that are relevant to health and wellbeing. Year 10 students have one Te Reo period a week for two terms. Students are able to choose from four topics (Tikanga, Kūpapa, Waiata and Ora). The programme is designed so that it can easily be adapted to suit students' interest, learning style and ability. Students are assessed on a continuous basis. The assessments are based on projects (Powerpoints, Presentations etc) and student portfolios. Page 30

Perceptions and Understandings of Māori Health and Wellbeing Why learn about health? Learning about health is a priority for the unit of learning. Contract law pertains to the specific terms and conditions involved in the supply of a particular product or service. On the other hand, tort law governs all business practices (Cornell 2011) It is based on unwritten common law, although it can be reinforced by statutes passed by the legislature. Aside from these statutes, court decisions are based on precedent, that is, previous cases involving similar facts. Strict liability was first introduced into the law of negligence in United States v Carroll Towing, Inc. (1954), a case involving a barge belonging to the defendant which had moored along the shores of a river. During the night, the barge became detached from its moorings and floated away. The plaintiffs owned several fishing nets that were attached to the barge and as a result of this, they lost their net. The defendant argued that in order to recover damages, the plaintiff had to prove that the defendant was negligent. Judge Cardozo ruled that under these circumstances, it is not necessary for the plaintiff to prove negligence as the defendant was liable. Strict liability is based on no fault liability, in that a person or business is liable for damages that result from an activity or condition, whether negligent or not (Cornell 2011). Strict liability is based on the idea that some activities are too dangerous, and therefore any damages caused by these activities should be paid even if no negligence was involved. For example, damages caused by defective products are strictly liable. In the law of negligence, strict liability is based on the concept of foreseeability (Cornell 2011). If a defendant has failed to foresee some consequences of an activity or condition, the defendant can be held liable even if there was no negligence involved. opening: “What you do speaks so loud that I cannot hear what you say.” – Ralph Waldo Emerson Whether you’re giving (or receiving) feedback, confronting a colleague, having a collaborative meeting, or just engaging in casual conversation, your body language matters. Body language alone can make or break a conversation. According to Psychologist World, human communication is 20% verbal and 80% non-verbal. Body language that doesn’t coincide with the message we intend to send can therefore lead to relationship ruptures, misunderstandings, and unwanted outcomes. Body language is the primary language of emotion, and how others perceive our emotion influences how our communication lands for them. A study by researchers at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and at New York University and
continuation:
published in The Journal of Neuroscience showed that when a person smiles while frowning, observers perceive the face as more negative than when they are not smiling. But when a person smiles without frowning, observers perceive the face as more positive. Your body language is part of who you are as a person and how others perceive you. It’s impossible to control body language, but it is possible to consciously manage it to more effectively convey the message you intend. Here are some guidelines to help with that. When you enter a room or a meeting, you have the opportunity to start in the right place by giving off positive vibes. When you greet others, open your body to them instead of guarding yourself and being closed off. Instead of folding your arms across your chest and placing your hands in your pockets, put them around your body and hold something. Place your feet shoulder-width apart with one foot slightly in front of the other. This open posture shows that you’re more approachable and welcoming. When you’re making a point or speaking to someone, make eye contact with them instead of scanning the room. You’ll notice that you have a more powerful impact on your audience when they have to focus on you and not be distracted by where you’re looking. If you find it difficult to maintain eye contact, try looking at the corner of their eyes, the bridge of their nose, or their lips. Your body posture while sitting and standing can make a huge difference to how others perceive you. Avoid slouching, crossing your legs with one knee pointing up and placing your feet under the chair – it can come across as defensive, aggressive, bored, or disinterested. Instead, try to maintain an upright and open posture that shows you’re engaged and interested. If you have your hands, you can place them on your hips or rest them on the table in front of you. When you’re speaking to someone, try to keep your hands and arms relaxed and away from your body. Hold something, if you need to. If you have an audience, move around a bit to show engagement and change up your energy level. If you’re giving feedback to a colleague, try not to make gestures that signal judgment (frowning, pursing your lips, rolling your eyes). Try instead to show empathy and support using open hand gestures. Take a look at the Master Class by Oprah Winfrey for some helpful body language tips. Stock Market Bubble Definition A stock market bubble refers to a situation where the prices of stocks rise to a point that is significantly higher than their fundamental values. It’s a market condition characterized by excessively high stock prices that are then followed by sharp declines and inevitable crashes. Stock Market Bubble Examples The credit bubble of 2007-2008 and the dot-com bubble (1995-2000) are among the most well-known and significant examples of stock market bubbles. The credit bubble was characterized by exorbitantly high housing prices and the proliferation of fraudulent subprime mortgages. This triggered a financial crisis in 2008 that led to a global recession. The dot-com bubble was driven by the exponential growth of the internet and overvaluation of tech stocks, especially those of companies with no real revenue or a path to profitability. Viruses such as West Nile and Zika can lead to an infection that continuously spreads and infiltrates the central nervous system, or CNS, which consists of the brain and spinal cord. Activation of the type I interferon (IFN) response — a feature of the innate immune response, the body’s
continuation: first line of defense against pathogens — is required to block viruses like the influenza virus from invading and spreading throughout the brain. IFNs are one of many molecules that make up part of this innate immune response. IFN signaling is one of the few natural ways to combat viruses. For decades, IFNs have been studied as potential treatments for viruses that make their way to the brain. Although some antiviral drugs can be successful against many of these pathogens, such as HIV or the common cold virus, there are others that have proved to be resistant. The team investigated a possible link between nGD and protection against viruses using a mouse model with the disease. They also looked at mice given injections of type I IFN to boost it levels in their bodies to see whether that would make them more resistant. The study showed that nGD mice were more resistant to infection by West Nile virus than controls and that this was due to an increase in IFN levels. Knocking out IFN signaling in nGD mice made them more susceptible to infection by West Nile virus, while boosting IFN signaling in control mice protected them against infection. A follow-up study is required to determine whether patients with nGD are more resistant to virus infections that spread to the brain. There are several psychological reasons why you may find decision-making difficult right now. First, there is a looming present threat. The disease is real. Around the world, people are dying from it and it is spreading rapidly enough that there is new news every day. Humans are wired to pay attention to threats, and so this story captures our attention in a way that a distant threat like climate change does not. Second, there is a lot of uncertainty about the spread of the virus —
continuation:

Although it is not easy to make good decisions right now, there are a few recommendations that can help you avoid some of the worst choices and make the most of the situation. Most importantly, don't rush into a decision that involves a large investment of resources, time, or money. If you really want to go on vacation, be patient — the situation is changing very quickly and you may well discover a better way of doing it if you can wait. Moreover, COVID-19 will be with us for months and possibly years as we figure out how to control it.

Between 1845 and 1852 over one million Irish peasants died of starvation and another million fled the country hoping for fuller bellies. While there were many political and social factors leading to the terrible scale of this tragedy, everything started with nearly 3 million Irish peasants subsisting on a single strain of plant in their fields, one variety of the potato. This great tragedy hits close to home here at Heritage Foods USA as we support farmers fighting against the pressure of moving toward

A Suggested Cure: Diversification into Traditional Farming Practices

The farmer who chooses to grow a single crop is called a monoculture farmer and their practices are referred to as monoculture. While there are some benefits to monoculture, especially in the industrial world of farming, there are also inherent dangers. One of the most significant is that by specializing in a single crop, monoculture farmers have sacrificed the protections that nature originally provided.

Every time we buy food we are casting a vote on the type of farmer, and the style of farming that we want to support. If we recognize the dangers of monoculture, we must vote against it and support farmers who grow as many varieties and crops as possible. Here are some ways to support traditional farmers:

Talk with your local farmer about the crops he grows and offer to buy some for yourself.

Refrain from buying food at large chains; farmers' markets are a better option.

Buy local, organic foods from farmers who avoid using pesticides (even if they are locally grown) and support sustainable farming practices.

Rotate crops on a schedule (this may involve growing a variety of different crops, so it works as an effective monoculture strategy).

Store crops by drying, canning and freezing. In doing so, you can preserve a crop that is in season for use throughout the year and limit the amount of space required to store fresh foods.

Prepare quality seeds for planting in the following season.

Moreover, the Fed has always been either celebrated or criticized for stepping in whenever the U.S. is stricken with some kind of fear. During the coronavirus outbreak, the central bank has unleashed a massive number of monetary easing tactics, which has prompted editors from Wikipedia to add updated information to the Fed’s Wiki page. The central bank’s page now states: “[the] COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 [has] led to the expansion of the roles and responsibilities of the Federal Reserve System.” Panic at the Knickerbocker Trust – 1907 During
continuation:
the first decade of the twentieth century, the U.S. banking and trust company sectors grew rapidly. Meanwhile, the Fed did not exist and there was no central bank to oversee these rapidly evolving institutions. However, in the fall of 1907, the absence of a central bank to stabilize the financial markets became painfully obvious. Investors started to panic and were quick to sell off their holdings of trust company stock. Consequently, the prices plummeted and many investors suffered great financial loss.
This initial panic resulted in two other major bankruptcies, but investors and bank officials continued to demand liquidity. In short order, the assets were sold off at prices that were much lower than expected and this further exacerbated the crisis. The Panic of 1907 brought to light the absence of a central bank for the U.S. At the time, there were several private banks that acted as de facto “lenders of last resort,” but they were incapable of handling the massive liquidity crisis that had gripped the financial markets. As a result, Congress created the Federal Reserve System with the express purpose of addressing liquidity crises in the U.S. financial system. The Federal Reserve was born – 1913 In May of 1913, both houses of Congress approved the creation of the Federal Reserve System. The Federal Reserve, a.k.a. “the Fed,” was established with the dual mandate of providing stability to the financial markets and fostering economic growth. The Federal Reserve System is made up of 12 regional banks that are supervised by the Board of Governors in Washington, D.C.
One of the most impressive parts of the Fed’s creation was the fact that it was a private-public partnership. The regional banks were established as private corporations, but they are “owned” by their member banks and they are required to follow the policies established by the Board of Governors. This unique combination of private and public entities is what gives the Fed so much power and flexibility to act in a crisis. The Federal Reserve has always been criticized for growing “too big to fail” and being unable to properly regulate the financial sector. Both of these complaints have come into sharp focus since the Fed’s creation. Still, the Federal Reserve is the most powerful central bank in history and it has become a hallmark of the U.S. financial system. The Fed today – COVID-19 crisis ever since 1913, the Federal Reserve has become an integral part of the U.S. financial system. In fact, it is more powerful and influential than any other central bank in the world. The Fed’s strength stems from its unique structure, which is a private-public partnership between 12 regional banks and the Board of Governors.
This hybrid structure allows the Fed to take decisive action during a crisis and gives it an enormous amount of flexibility to respond to changing conditions. However, the Fed has always been criticized for being “too big to fail” and for not properly regulating the financial system. These concerns have come into sharp focus since the Fed’s creation, but they will likely never go away. In recent months, the coronavirus pandemic has caused an unprecedented crisis in the financial markets and the Fed has stepped in to provide liquidity and stability.

The Magi, the Wise Men (Matthew 2.1-12): Who were they? What did they seek? Matthew is building up the story of Jesus. He has written the genealogy (Matthew 1:1-17) and summarised the birth of Jesus (1:18-25), before moving on to the arrival of the magi (2:1-12). The story about the wise men in a foreign land, seeking Jesus as King of the Jews, is his way of introducing him to us (the readers). Matthew has already told us that he was born in Bethlehem, not Jerusalem. That city, the political capital of Judah, is where David had lived and reigned as King and was the location for many important events in Israel’s history. This, then, is why they had travelled there – to find the newborn King. But instead, they found not the infant but just a house with the child sleeping in a creche (2:11). opening: The sun is rising on a new era for renewable energy in Gainesville, Fla. Starting this month, residents and business owners with solar panels connected to the power grid will get a monthly check from their city-owned electric utility, the result of a first-in-the-nation policy called a feed-in tariff. The new policy essentially turns privately owned rooftop solar panels into micro power generators for the utility. The city will pay up to 32 cents per kilowatt-hour for power they generate over the next 20 years, delivering their owners about a 5 percent profit over the equipment's lifespan. Feed-in tariffs like this have long been the primary tool for financing renewable energy projects in Europe, and they are a reason Spain
continuation:
, Germany and France have gone far ahead of the U.S. in renewable energy installations. The city council for Gainesville approved its feed-in tariff last month, and it now joins Portland (Ore.), Boulder (Colo.) and Berkeley (Calif.) as cities to offer payments to their solar panel owners. The concept of the tariff is simple: A city or utility will buy power produced by a citizen or business owner and pay them according to the price it sells the same power on the grid. Some utilities have capped the amount they will pay, typically 20 cents per kilowatt-hour or lower, but Gainesville's goes up to 32 cents per kWh. The city limits the amount of power each solar panel owner can sell to 10 kilowatts, which is typically the amount of power an average house needs. This helps to ensure that solar panels are used in a decentralized way, with energy generated where it's used. Although the concept is simple, there are some challenges with feed-in tariffs that will require time and study before it becomes a mainstay of renewable energy financing.

continuation: the Border Collie, a breed that would go on to redefine the standards of canine herding through its unmatched intelligence and intense eye. opening: It’s safe to say that by now, most of us understand the importance of protecting our planet from environmental harm. We recycle, buy reusable water bottles, and donate items rather than throw them away. Some people take it even further and drive electric cars, use solar energy, and shop with businesses that have an eco-friendly mindset. But let’s face it, many of us are busy – and while we want to do our part, we want our contributions to be simple and practical. If you want to do more to help save the planet without too much work on your end, there are some simple changes you can make. They require a little effort upfront, but nothing over the top.
continuation:
First, consider what you eat and how you get to school or work. Instead of relying on your car for every trip, try walking, biking, or carpooling when possible; even short distances add up to significant carbon savings over time. At the grocery store, pack your own bag and strictly stick to a shopping list to avoid impulse buys that often end up in the trash. When preparing meals, reduce your meat intake or try plant-based options a few times a week, as livestock production is a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions.

On the topic of home life, switch your household lighting to LEDs immediately, as they last longer and use far less energy than traditional bulbs. Unplug electronics when you aren't using them, or invest in a smart power strip to cut down on "vampire power" that drains energy even when devices are turned off. Finally, wash your clothes in cold water and air-dry them whenever the weather permits; this simple adjustment can drastically lower your energy consumption while still keeping your wardrobe fresh and durable.

opening: Warehousing is often regarded as a necessary evil that needs to be marginalized, if not eliminated. Apparently, the distribution center only incurred costs and increased response times. The organization immediately decided to terminate the distribution center. In most instances the distribution center does add value to the supply chain. Hence, it is important to understand
continuation: the specific conditions under which warehousing remains a critical component versus when it acts as an inefficient bottleneck. Factors such as product perishability, the need for bulk-breaking to meet varied customer demands, high transportation costs relative to inventory holding costs, and the requirement for value-added services like kitting or quality inspection often dictate whether a facility should be retained. By analyzing these variables, supply chain managers can strategically optimize their networks, ensuring that warehousing is utilized only where it generates tangible value in cost reduction, service level improvement, or inventory risk mitigation.

opening: Over 100 million Americans have high blood pressure. This is concerning because high blood pressure can lead to cardiovascular disease, which is the leading cause of death worldwide. The easiest way to prevent this is to monitor your blood pressure and take steps to reduce it. The first question many people ask is, how often should you take your blood pressure? You want to monitor your blood pressure, but you also want accurate measurements. This guide will help you understand the ins and outs of taking your blood pressure. How Often Should You Take Your Blood Pressure The frequency that you test your blood pressure will depend on your health history. At a minimum, you should have your blood pressure
continuation: checked by a healthcare professional once or twice a year, unless your provider advises otherwise due to existing conditions or medication. For individuals who have been diagnosed with high blood pressure, monitoring becomes much more critical; you should check your blood pressure at home several times a week to ensure it remains within a safe range. If your readings are consistently below the recommended threshold (typically 120/80 mmHg), you may visit your doctor once annually. However, if your home readings are persistently elevated, follow-up visits should be scheduled immediately. It is important to remember that blood pressure can fluctuate throughout the day, so taking readings at different times—such as in the morning upon waking and in the evening before bed—can provide a more comprehensive picture of your cardiovascular health. Always sit quietly for five minutes before measuring, ensure your back is supported and feet are flat on the floor, and keep a log of your results to share with your doctor during your next appointment.

opening: TORTS Cyber Torts, Strict Liability, Products Liability, Consumer Protection Introduction The business world is governed largely by 2 types of law, contract law and tort law. Contract law pertains to the specific terms and conditions involved in the supply of a particular product or service. On the other hand, tort law governs all business practices (Cornell 2011) It is based on unwritten common law, although it can be reinforced by statutes passed by the legislature. Aside from these statutes, court decisions are based on precedent, that is, previous cases involving similar facts. Torts are wrongs committed against individuals and groups and can be intentional or unintentional. Intentional torts are wrongs done deliberately and therefore criminal and dealt with by criminal
continuation: law, whereas unintentional torts, also known as negligence or strict liability cases, arise from accidents or failures to meet a duty of care. Within the realm of torts, cyber torts have emerged as a critical area of concern in the digital age, encompassing violations such as invasion of privacy, defamation online, and intellectual property infringement committed through electronic means. These digital wrongs often transcend geographical boundaries, creating complex litigation challenges for businesses operating in global markets. Closely related to these are areas of strict liability and products liability, where a party may be held responsible for damages regardless of fault, particularly when defective products cause harm to consumers. Finally, consumer protection laws serve as statutory safeguards designed to ensure fair trade practices, preventing deceptive acts and ensuring that businesses adhere to standards of honesty and safety in their dealings with the public.

opening: “What you do speaks so loud that I cannot hear what you say.” – Ralph Waldo Emerson Whether you’re giving (or receiving) feedback, confronting a colleague, having a collaborative meeting, or just engaging in casual conversation, your body language matters. Body language alone can make or break a conversation. According to Psychologist World, human communication is 20% verbal and 80% non-verbal. Body language that doesn’t coincide with the message we intend to send can therefore lead to relationship ruptures, misunderstandings, and unwanted outcomes. Body language is the primary language of emotion, and how others perceive our emotion influences how our communication lands for them. A study by researchers at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and at New York University and
continuation: A study by researchers at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and at New York University and Stanford University found that listeners are far better at detecting emotional states from body language than from spoken words alone. Specifically, when people hear a recording of someone's voice saying "I'm sad," they may initially feel the sadness, but when they watch a video where the speaker says the same words while laughing or smiling with tension, their brain quickly detects the incongruity. This mismatch triggers skepticism, causing the listener to dismiss the verbal message and rely more heavily on the non-verbal cues. Consequently, if your tone is warm but your arms are crossed or your eyes are averted, the recipient will perceive you as cold or dismissive, regardless of what words you chose. To ensure your message is received as intended, it is crucial to align your posture, facial expressions, and gestures with your verbal intent. By practicing this alignment before important conversations, you can build trust and prevent the disconnect that leads to conflict.

opening: Types of Financial Bubbles & Their Impact on the Stock Market Information is critical for all investors, and this is particularly true for anyone interested in stocks. Investing in stock is a lucrative venture and is one of the ways to earn huge profits. However, the prices of stocks keep on shifting – bubbles and crashes are also common. And you must understand how to forecast price changes to benefit from your investment. There are different types of Financial Bubbles, read this post for more details What is the Financial Bubble? A bubble is an economic cycle, usually an uptick in the value of a financial asset. The price tag isn’t a true reflection of the actual cost. Bubbles occur
continuation:
when market sentiment becomes overly optimistic, driving prices to levels far exceeding the underlying fundamental value of the asset. This phenomenon is often fueled by speculation, herd behavior, and easy credit conditions rather than genuine economic improvement. As asset prices rise, they attract more investors who assume the trend will continue indefinitely, creating a self-reinforcing cycle of inflation that detaches the market from reality. Eventually, however, the bubble must burst when new data reveals that the asset's price cannot be sustained, leading to a rapid and severe correction known as a crash.

Here are the most common types of financial bubbles and their specific impacts on the stock market:

**1. The Dot-Com Bubble (2000)**
This bubble centered around internet-related companies during the late 1990s. Investors poured money into any company with a website or an ".com" in its name, regardless of whether those companies had profits or even products. Stock prices for tech giants soared to astronomical heights before the market realized many of these businesses were worthless. The subsequent crash wiped out trillions in market value and forced many players, like Enron and WorldCom, into bankruptcy, causing the S&P 500 to lose nearly half its value in just a few years.

**2. The Housing Bubble (2008)**
While technically centered on real estate, this bubble had a catastrophic ripple effect on the stock market. Rising home prices and excessive lending led to the subprime mortgage crisis. As homeowners defaulted on loans, financial institutions holding these assets collapsed. The ensuing credit crunch froze the global economy, causing the stock market to enter its longest bear market in history until 2013, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average losing over 50% of its value from its peak.

**3. The Technology and AI Bubble (Recent Years)**
Current market dynamics show signs of a new bubble driven by artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks. While innovation is real, the current valuations for many AI-related companies suggest expectations of revenue and profitability that are impossible to meet in the short term. If these high-growth stocks continue to rise on hype alone, they face a sharp correction that could drag down the entire technology sector and lower overall market indices like the Nasdaq.

Understanding these patterns allows investors to distinguish between a healthy rally driven by fundamentals and an unsustainable bubble. By monitoring valuation metrics, such as the P/E ratio relative to historical averages and earnings growth, investors can identify when prices are becoming detached from reality, helping them protect their portfolios before the inevitable crash.

opening: Neuronopathic Gaucher disease (nGD) induces an immune response that protects against viral infections in the brain, according to an early study in animals. Understanding how this happens and whether GD patients are more resistant to infection needs further studies, scientists said. Viruses such as West Nile and Zika can lead to an infection that continuously spreads and infiltrates the central nervous system, or CNS, which consists of the brain and spinal cord. Some of these viruses, such as those that are insect-borne, often are resistant to treatment. This drives the need to identify which biological processes affect the outcomes of those infections. Activation of the type I interferon (IFN) response — a feature of the innate immune response, the body’s
continuation: first line of defense against pathogens — is often a key indicator of a robust immune reaction. In the context of nGD, researchers observed that the accumulation of glucosylceramide due to the enzyme deficiency paradoxically triggers this interferon pathway, creating a barrier that prevents certain neurotropic viruses from establishing a foothold in neural tissue. While the precise mechanisms remain to be fully elucidated in humans, these animal models suggest that the chronic inflammatory state inherent to nGD could offer a dual-edged sword: potentially shielding vulnerable brain regions from viral neuroinvasion, while simultaneously increasing the risk of long-term neurological complications. Consequently, clinicians are now exploring whether the unique immunological landscape of Gaucher patients might influence their susceptibility to emerging CNS pathogens, prompting a reevaluation of risk stratification and therapeutic strategies for viral encephalitis in this population.

opening: By: Steve Northcutt What is the definition of marriage? What is marriage? In Websters Dictionary marriage is defined as the institution whereby men and women are joined in special kind of social and legal dependence for the purpose of founding and maintaining a family. Marriage has always been an evolving institution, bent and shaped by the historical moment and the needs and demands of its participants (Johnson 266). The Romans recognized the phenomenon we call
continuation: marriage as *conventio in facies*—the "meeting of faces"—which was essentially a contract between two parties of different sexes for the purpose of procreation and maintaining order within the household (Johnson 266). However, for the Romans, this bond was not indissoluble in the modern sense; under certain circumstances, a husband could simply leave his wife without formal legal proceedings, provided she was of childbearing age and he had fulfilled his financial obligations to her. It wasn't until later in the imperial period, particularly during the reign of Justinian, that marriage became more rigid and legally binding as a sacrament-like union, yet even then, the primary focus remained on the continuation of the family line and the legal authority (*patria potestas*) of the male head over the female spouse. This historical fluidity suggests that the strict binary and permanence we often attribute to marriage today are relatively recent developments in the broader human story of partnership.

opening: What idea quickly comes to mind when the word “accountant” gets mentioned in a conversation? Number crunching; charts. However, accountants do much more than just crunch numbers. As an accounting student, chances are you’ll need some accounting assignment help to improve your writing skills. You likely see yourself as a technical person (and you are) who don’t need to say or write much. And that would be the case if accountants didn’t have to communicate their numbers. But they do. Good communication skills can dramatically help your career as an accountant. Accounting is a Technical Discipline that Requires a Straight to-the-point Approach Accountants use both words and numbers to get their message across. As they prepare business letters, memos and
continuation: reports, they must distill complex financial data into clear, actionable insights for stakeholders who may not have a background in accounting. This means avoiding unnecessary jargon and focusing on the bottom line of what the numbers actually mean for the business. Whether you are explaining a variance in profit margins or justifying an expense to management, your message needs to be concise and evidence-based. In the professional world, ambiguity is often viewed as incompetence, so accountants are trained to be precise. You need to be able to translate your technical findings into a narrative that non-accountants can understand and trust. By mastering this balance between rigorous data analysis and crisp communication, you position yourself as a versatile asset capable of bridging the gap between finance departments and executive leadership.

opening: Gorongosa turns into a virtual water world during the rainy season and that is good for our hippos! Gorongosa was home to about 3,500 hippos in the 1970’s and they did a good job mowing the grasses of the Lake Urema floodplain. Today, Gorongosa has about 440 hippos but that is up from about 100 hippos in 2000. Hippos weigh up to 3.5 tons, which makes them the third-largest land mammal in the world after elephants and white rhinos. Hippos are amphibious – they spend most of their day resting and socializing in the water, and most of the night eating grass on land. An adult hippo can walk up to 5 miles or more from the water looking for
continuation: food. Their massive size and blunt snouts are not designed for long-distance grazing like deer or antelope, but rather for stripping vegetation along riverbanks and lake shores. Despite their aquatic preference, hippos can move surprisingly fast on land—reaching speeds of up to 30 miles per hour for short bursts—allowing them to cover that distance if necessary, though they typically stay closer to the water for safety from predators. Today's recovery of the hippo population in Gorongosa is a testament to successful conservation efforts, reversing a near-collapse driven by poaching and habitat loss during the civil war era.

opening: Have you been brushing your teeth the right way? There are many bad tooth brushing habits that you might have developed over the years without even knowing. Next time you brush your teeth, take a moment and think about how you’re brushing. Here are some common mistakes: Rushing the brush: Not brushing long enough You might be rushing your brush without even realizing it. Brushing for too short of a time means your teeth don’t get as clean as they should be. You should be brushing your teeth for at least 2 minutes, but 3 is even better. You might want to set a timer to see how long you’re spending brushing your teeth. Many electric toothbrushes also shut off
continuation: after 2 minutes to remind you. Another major error is brushing back and forth vigorously like scrubbing a floor. This aggressive horizontal motion can wear down your enamel and irritate your gums, potentially leading to gum recession and sensitivity. Instead, use a gentle, circular motion or small vibrations, especially along the gumline where plaque tends to accumulate. Don't forget to clean the back surfaces of your teeth; many people skip these because they are harder to reach, yet neglecting them can lead to cavities and gum disease on the very last molar. Additionally, avoid brushing immediately after eating acidic foods or drinks like coffee, soda, or citrus fruits. The acid temporarily softens your enamel, and brushing right away can cause microscopic abrasions; wait at least 30 minutes for your saliva to neutralize the acid and remineralize your teeth before you brush. Finally, remember to change your toothbrush every three to four months, or sooner if the bristles become frayed, as a worn-out brush won't clean effectively and can harm your gums.

opening: The news about the spread of COVID-19 is changing fast — and people are trying to make decisions about everything from whether to cancel vacations to how to best protect themselves and their communities. There are several psychological reasons why you may find decision-making difficult right now. First, there is a looming present threat. The disease is real. Around the world, people are dying from it and it is spreading rapidly enough that there is new news every day. Humans are wired to pay attention to threats, and so this story captures our attention in a way that a distant threat like climate change does not. Second, there is a lot of uncertainty about the spread of the virus —
continuation: we do not yet know exactly how long the disease will persist or with what severity it might affect us personally. This ambiguity creates anxiety because our brains crave predictability; when faced with unknown variables, we often freeze or oscillate between impulsive action and inaction. Third, there is a high emotional load associated with the pandemic, as grief over lost loved ones, fear of infection, and frustration over restrictions compete for our cognitive resources, leaving less mental bandwidth for careful deliberation. These factors combined can lead to decision fatigue, where the sheer volume of choices—from which mask to wear to whether to open a restaurant—paralyzes individuals, making it harder to act consistently despite knowing what is best.

opening: The history of Irish food is interesting for more than just the delicious combinations of meat, potatoes and alcohol but also for the lessons we must learn from the great tragedy of the Irish Potato Famine. Between 1845 and 1852 over one million Irish peasants died of starvation and another million fled the country hoping for fuller bellies. While there were many political and social factors leading to the terrible scale of this tragedy, everything started with nearly 3 million Irish peasants subsisting on a single strain of plant in their fields, one variety of the potato. This great tragedy hits close to home here at Heritage Foods USA as we support farmers fighting against the pressure of moving toward
continuation: diversified agricultural systems that can withstand economic and climate shocks. In an era where supply chains are increasingly volatile and extreme weather events threaten global food security, relying on monocultures proves dangerously fragile. Just as the Irish learned that a single crop cannot sustain a nation's future, Heritage Foods USA champions regenerative farming practices that prioritize soil health, crop rotation, and local resilience. By supporting farmers who grow a wide variety of native and heirloom produce, we help build a food system that is not only nutritious but also sustainable, ensuring that no family ever faces the horror of famine again.

opening: The Federal Reserve System was created after the “Panic of 1907” and ever since its inception in 1913, the Fed is one of the most powerful modern central banks in the world. Moreover, the Fed has always been either celebrated or criticized for stepping in whenever the U.S. is stricken with some kind of fear. During the coronavirus outbreak, the central bank has unleashed a massive number of monetary easing tactics, which has prompted editors from Wikipedia to add updated information to the Fed’s Wiki page. The central bank’s page now states: “[the] COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 [has] led to the expansion of the roles and responsibilities of the Federal Reserve System.” Panic at the Knickerbocker Trust – 1907 During
continuation: Panic at the Knickerbocker Trust – 1907 During that turbulent autumn, financial anxiety had already begun to grip New York City as rumors swirled about the stability of major institutions. The Knickerbocker Trust Company, a prominent holding firm with nearly $100 million in deposits, stood as a looming threat; its potential failure was believed to have already undermined confidence in the entire banking sector. As depositors rushed to withdraw their savings, a self-fulfilling prophecy threatened to ignite a full-blown financial collapse across the nation. Recognizing the impending catastrophe, influential financiers, including J.P. Morgan and Charles D. Norton, convened secretly to organize a rescue effort. They arranged for the Treasury Department to provide emergency silver certificates and simultaneously orchestrated a massive cash infusion by borrowing from other banks to prop up the failing trust. This coordinated intervention temporarily stabilized the market, but only after the authorities realized that no single regulatory body existed to manage such systemic crises. The sheer scale of the panic and the ad-hoc nature of the rescue efforts underscored a critical flaw in America's financial architecture, ultimately convincing President Theodore Roosevelt and Congress that a permanent central bank was essential to prevent such chaos from recurring in the future.

By Chris WittsTuesday 17 Nov 2020Morning Devotions with Chris Witts The name of Jesus Christ has become an expletive uttered almost everywhere in the Western world. Hollywood movies often mention Jesus in an unflattering way. Television, too, plays a big part. It’s no longer unusual to hear the name of Jesus shouted in programs—from soapies to chat shows. You hear it on the sporting field, in the street, at pubs and clubs, at work—in fact almost everywhere. Most of us have, apparently, accepted it as part of the standard English vocabulary. Even though a British Broadcasting Standards Commission (replaced in 2003 by Ofcom) report found that swearing and offensive language were a turn-off for
continuation: viewers, yet the exclusion of the name in a polite broadcast is often viewed by comedians and producers as a censorship exercise rather than a moral imperative. This paradox reveals how deeply entrenched the habit has become; the word has lost its sacred weight and gained the utility of a punchline, a filler, or an emotional release valve. Consequently, the reaction to its use is less about offense regarding blasphemy and more about annoyance at the breach of social etiquette, creating a unique cultural space where the divine name is simultaneously ubiquitous and banal. As the report concluded, while some audiences might find such language off-putting, the pervasive nature of this linguistic shift suggests that for many in modern society, the name of Jesus is simply another brick in the wall of everyday conversation, stripped of its original reverence but retained for its rhythmic impact.

opening: The sun is rising on a new era for renewable energy in Gainesville, Fla. Starting this month, residents and business owners with solar panels connected to the power grid will get a monthly check from their city-owned electric utility, the result of a first-in-the-nation policy called a feed-in tariff. The new policy essentially turns privately owned rooftop solar panels into micro power generators for the utility. The city will pay up to 32 cents per kilowatt-hour for power they generate over the next 20 years, delivering their owners about a 5 percent profit over the equipment's lifespan. Feed-in tariffs like this have long been the primary tool for financing renewable energy projects in Europe, and they are a reason Spain
continuation: and Germany became global leaders in solar adoption. In the United States, however, such incentives have been historically rare, often stifled by federal tax credits that expire or limited state-level rebates. By establishing this program, Gainesville is positioning itself as a national model for local governments aiming to support decentralized energy production without relying on federal legislation. The initiative not only accelerates the city's transition toward sustainable power but also creates a new revenue stream for homeowners, effectively turning residential property into a mini-utility that contributes directly to the community's grid stability. As neighboring states look to replicate the success of this pilot program, the experiment in Gainesville marks a pivotal moment in the democratization of America's energy landscape.

opening: Murali Krishna Gumma, the head of GIS and Remote Sensing Lab at ICRISAT, co-authored a new paper that demonstrated the power of continental-scale mapping using 30-meter Landsat imagery data on Google Earth Engine. Applying the random forest machine learning algorithm, the team, led by Pardhasaradhi Teluguntla at U. S. Geological Survey, was able to generate the new cropland extent in Australia and China with the overall accuracy exceeding 94%. The data products are freely available from the USGS website at https://lpdaac.usgs.gov/node/1282. Mapping high resolution (30-m or better) cropland extent over very large areas such as continents or large countries or regions accurately, precisely, repeatedly, and rapidly is of great importance for addressing the global food and water security challenges. Such
continuation: a large-scale mapping can enable crop production mapping, areal estimation, crop yield forecasting, evaluation of irrigation and water-use efficiency, and risk assessment of crop production. However, mapping cropland extent over large areas using high resolution data has been a major challenge due to the lack of a cost-effective data processing pipeline and difficulty in identifying crops from coarser resolution land cover data. Also, accessing large-scale high resolution satellite imagery is a challenge itself. Google Earth Engine Cloud platform, a cloud-based platform for accessing large-scale geo-spatial datasets, can help overcome the above-mentioned challenges. Our recent study demonstrates how a machine learning technique, random forest, is used to classify cropland using 30-m spatial resolution Landsat imagery available on Google Earth Engine and how the large-scale cropland extent maps are generated for Australia and China with the overall accuracy exceeding 94%. These cropland products are freely available from the USGS website at https://lpdaac.usgs.gov/node/1282.

opening: In the world of working stock dogs, there is no more iconic breed than the border collie. The quintessential sheepdog, the border collie can trace its ancestry to rough drover’s dogs used in the border country between England and Scotland from the 17th to the 19th century to work livestock and drive them to market. Despite being indispensable to the shepherds of these rugged and inhospitable highlands, the drover dogs of this era were neither easy to handle nor easy on the stock. In the late 19th century, a shepherd by the name of Adam Telfer began experimenting with a cross between these coarse dogs and the milder-mannered working collie. The end result was a dog by the name of
continuation:
Old Cockie, who fathered a line of more manageable sheep dogs with the requisite willingness to work sheep. It was Old Cockie’s grandson, Wiston Cap, whose progeny founded the modern border collie breed in the 1900s. The modern border collie continues to be revered for its versatility, intelligence, and eagerness to please, and is the most popular working sheepdog in the world.

Border collies are a herding dog at heart and enjoy being challenged. As such, they are happiest in a home where they have plenty of room to roam, with a fenced yard or access to a large field being preferable to an apartment. Border collies are more inclined to roam than many other breeds, and are known for their ability to jump tall fences, so they require a secure yard and close supervision. Border collies also have a long, coarse coat that makes them unsuitable for indoors, as their fur tends to shed profusely. They’re also prone to excessive barking, which can upset the neighbors. This makes them unsuitable for apartment-dwelling.

Border collies are also prone to separation anxiety, and they need a lot of attention and stimulation to keep them happy. They’re not suitable for a family that will be away from the house for a long period.

opening: It’s safe to say that by now, most of us understand the importance of protecting our planet from environmental harm. We recycle, buy reusable water bottles, and donate items rather than throw them away. Some people take it even further and drive electric cars, use solar energy, and shop with businesses that have an eco-friendly mindset. But let’s face it, many of us are busy – and while we want to do our part, we want our contributions to be simple and practical. If you want to do more to help save the planet without too much work on your end, there are some simple changes you can make. They require a little effort upfront, but nothing over the top.

If you’re ready to join the fight and be a planet protector, here are seven tips to get you started.

Wrap Your Pipes in Insulation

One of the biggest threats to our planet is global warming. We often think of the warming of the Earth as something that’s caused by the air outside, but did you know that your plumbing system can contribute to the problem? It’s true – leaky pipes and poorly insulated lines can cause unwanted heat loss. To combat the problem, pipe wrapping insulation is necessary to keep heat in. Without that extra layer of protection, the pipes will lose heat to the surrounding environment, which results in more energy being used to keep the pipes warm enough to function. While the loss of energy itself isn’t much of a threat to the environment, it’s the extra energy needed to keep the pipes warm that causes the issue. Every time your pipes lose heat, your system will automatically turn on to heat them back up again, which causes more emissions to be released into the air. Pipe insulation may seem like a simple change, but by using pipe wrapping insulation, you’ll reduce energy loss, which can help keep the planet cool.

Purchase a Water Heater Timer

Another way to save energy is to purchase a water heater timer. Most water heaters turn on and off throughout the day to keep the water hot, and they tend to stay on for much longer than necessary. Unfortunately, that means more energy is being wasted. Thankfully, there’s a simple solution to the problem: water heater timers. These devices allow you to set the times when you want your water heater to turn on and off. For example, you can choose to have it on from 6 am to 10 am and 6 pm to 10 pm if that’s when you use hot water the most. By choosing your own times, you’re able to reduce the amount of energy being wasted and ensure that your water heater only uses what’s necessary.

Recycle Your Electronics

Most of us are familiar with recycling our paper, plastic, and aluminum products, but what about electronics? It may seem like a simple step, but recycling your old or broken electronics can help protect the planet. Electronics contain many different metals and components that can be harmful to the environment if not recycled properly. By bringing your unwanted electronic items to a recycling center, you’re ensuring that they’ll be disposed of correctly and that the materials will be used to create new products. Some electronics may even be refurbished and resold, which is an added bonus for the environment.

Unplug Your Devices

Many of us fall into the habit of leaving our electronics plugged in, even when they’re not in use. Unfortunately, this can lead to wasted energy and more carbon emissions. When plugged in, devices still draw electricity even when they’re turned off or in standby mode. To combat this issue, try unplugging your devices when they’re not in use. opening: Warehousing is often regarded as a necessary evil that needs to be marginalized, if not eliminated. Although, we strongly disagree with this point of view in general, occasionally the value of warehousing might be redundant as demonstrated by the following case study. Case Study: Office Supplies for Non-profit Organization A non-profit organization held a central inventory of office supplies. A study revealed that it would be cheaper and quicker if the various branches ordered the office supplies directly from the wholesaler. Apparently, the distribution center only incurred costs and increased response times. The organization immediately decided to terminate the distribution center. In most instances the distribution center does add value to the supply chain. Hence, it is important to understand

It takes some time to deliver supplies from the warehouse to the distribution center and then onwards to the final customer. This lead time reduces the responsiveness of the supply chain to changes in customer demand. The distribution center becomes obsolete when the additional costs of carrying higher inventory levels exceed the benefits of shorter delivery times. 2 The distribution center has also been shown to incur an additional inventory cost due to the lack of direct connection between production and customers. However, it is possible to mitigate this disadvantage by using storage practices such as frequent deliveries, or by connecting the distribution center directly to production. The distribution center needs to be located near the final customer in order to avoid the additional costs of the distribution center. Hence, the distribution center might add value only when it is located at the final delivery point or at one of the nodes along the final delivery path. The distribution center might also add value when it is located near a primary warehouse.
